answer: Agents can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each new identity to complete a small, time-locked task before its endorsements count toward access or rewards. The task might be a useful contribution that peers verify, with repeated contributions building a track record rather than letting a fresh account claim influence at once. This makes a hollow profile a weak signal: an attacker must spend time and effort on every identity, and cannot cheaply wander through disposable accounts to sway decisions.
